## 1. Executive Summary

The Histopathology System is a business-critical ASP.NET WebForms application running on .NET Framework 4.0 / IIS / Windows Server. It manages the complete lifecycle of pathology submissions — from customer receipt through histology processing, reporting, and archiving — for Crown Commercial Property laboratory operations. It has been in continuous use with no significant architectural change.

The migration programme transitions the system to a **C# 14 / .NET 10 Modular Monolith** deployed as a container on **Azure App Service**, with **Azure Entra ID** authentication, **Dapper + stored procedures** data access, **HTML/PDF reports** (via `pdf-report-modernizer.agent`), and **Application Insights** observability.

This document defines the programme structure — objectives, roadmap, team, governance, and success criteria — to maximise delivery success probability against the industry-standard failure patterns identified in the Chaos Report.

### Why this migration is necessary

| Driver | Detail |
|---|---|
| Platform end-of-support | .NET Framework 4.0 is out of mainstream support; no security patches post-2016 |
| IIS / Windows Server hosting | On-premises IIS hosting incurs ongoing infrastructure cost and operational risk |
| Authentication risk | Windows Authentication is not compatible with Azure App Service hosting model |
| Crystal Reports dependency | Crystal Reports 13 GAC installation is incompatible with .NET 5+ and container deployment |
| Zero test coverage | 185 VB source files with no automated tests; any change carries silent regression risk |
| Scalability ceiling | InProc session state pins the system to a single IIS instance; no horizontal scaling possible |

### What the migration does NOT do

- **No database schema changes.** All stored procedures, tables, and indexes are frozen. The database is the stable anchor throughout migration.
- **No functional redesign.** Business rules (PG-number auto-reversal, histology ref types, batch status lifecycle, role-based access) are translated verbatim.
- **No big-bang rewrite.** Delivery is structured in 6 phases, each independently deployable and reversible.

## 2. Migration Objectives

| # | Objective | Measurable Success Criterion |
|---|---|---|
| O-1 | Eliminate .NET Framework 4.0 dependency | New solution compiles and runs on .NET 10 with zero legacy framework references |
| O-2 | Replace Windows Authentication with Entra ID | All three role groups (`Customer`, `Histopathology User`, `Maintenance`) sign in via Entra ID; zero access widening |
| O-3 | Replace Crystal Reports with HTML/PDF rendering | All 9 reports pass RMSE pixel diff validation against Phase 0 reference baselines |
| O-4 | Eliminate IIS / Windows Server hosting dependency | Application deploys and runs correctly on Azure App Service Linux container |
| O-5 | Achieve automated test coverage of all domain logic | Histo.Tests CI suite passes green; critical business rules have named unit test cases |
| O-6 | Remove plaintext SQL credential from source control | `Web.config` credential eliminated; replaced with Managed Identity + Key Vault reference |
| O-7 | Establish observable, supportable production platform | Application Insights exception telemetry active; structured logging via Serilog; health check endpoint returns 200 |
| O-8 | Preserve complete functional equivalence | Automated E2E baseline suite passes against the migrated application before production cutover |

## 3. Chaos Report Risk Mitigation — How This Programme Is Designed to Succeed

The Chaos Report (Standish Group) identifies the following as the most common causes of IT project failure. Each is addressed explicitly in this programme design.

| Failure pattern | Probability without mitigation | This programme's mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| **Incomplete requirements** | High | `docs/HLD.md` and `docs/LLD.md` document the full current-state system before any change begins. Migration-Plan.md defines exact deliverables per phase. |
| **Lack of user involvement** | High | Each phase has a defined UAT gate requiring sign-off from a named representative from the laboratory team. Phase 5 UI batches are validated by end-users before the next batch begins. |
| **Lack of executive support** | High | Executive sponsor is a named role in the team model (see `docs/Intelligent-Team-Model.md`) with defined decision authority at each phase gate. |
| **Lack of resources / skills** | Medium | AI augmentation (GitHub Copilot, M365 Copilot) is embedded in every developer and QA role, increasing effective throughput. VB.NET-to-C# conversion skill gap is mitigated by `dotnet-framework-upgrade` agent. |
| **Unrealistic expectations** | Medium | This plan provides phase-level estimates, not a single delivery date. Each phase has independent exit criteria. Stakeholders review estimates at each gate, not just at the start. |
| **Changing requirements** | Medium | The "database is frozen" principle locks the scope anchor. Feature changes are deferred to a post-migration backlog and must not enter any active migration phase. |
| **Inadequate planning** | Low (mitigated) | Six-phase roadmap with explicit entry criteria, exit criteria, rollback strategy, and dependency mapping per phase. No phase begins without human approval. |
| **Unreliable technology** | Low (mitigated) | Technology choices (Dapper, Razor Pages, HTMX, HTML/PDF rendering) are production-proven and specifically selected for compatibility with the .NET 10 stack and the Azure App Service hosting model. |

### Phase 1 — Solution Scaffold + Infrastructure Module

**Duration:** 3 weeks  
**Purpose:** Create the new .NET 10 solution structure and shared infrastructure layer. No business logic.

**Key deliverables:**
- `HistopathologySystem.slnx` with 9 project stubs
- `Histo.Infrastructure`: `IDbConnectionFactory`, `IAppLogger`, `AppOptions`
- `Histo.Web` stub: `Program.cs`, `/health` endpoint, `_Layout.cshtml` stub
- Integration tests: SQL connection factory, options binding

**Go/no-go gate:** `GET /health` returns 200 from the containerised application in the dev environment. CI green.

---

### Phase 2 — Authentication Migration

**Duration:** 3 weeks (can overlap with Phase 3)  
**Purpose:** Replace Windows Authentication with Azure Entra ID.

**Key deliverables:**
- `Microsoft.Identity.Web` wired in `Program.cs`
- Three authorisation policies mapped to Entra group claims
- `ISessionService.CurrentUser` populated with UserID, GroupName, AreaName
- Auth smoke test: sign-in round-trip, role claim present, session populated

**Critical dependency:** Entra ID app registration and group ID confirmation from Azure admin (see Section 5 — Human-in-the-Loop steps).

**Go/no-go gate:** Auth equivalence test suite passes. No access widening. `ISS-009` (NT login format mapping) resolved.

---

### Phase 3 — Reporting Migration (Crystal Reports → PDF)

**Duration:** 4 weeks (runs in parallel with Phase 2)  
**Purpose:** Replace all 9 Crystal Reports with HTML/PDF rendering via `pdf-report-modernizer.agent`.

**Key deliverables:**
- PDF rendering service + base layout
- 7 low/medium complexity reports converted
- `HistologyReport` + `HistologySubReport` converted (manual ViewModel design required)
- All 9 reports pass RMSE pixel diff validation against Phase 0 reference PDFs

**Go/no-go gate:** All 9 reports pass within 5% RMSE threshold.

---

### Phase 4 — Domain and Repository Modules

**Duration:** 6 weeks  
**Purpose:** Convert each `HistopathologyLib` domain class to C# POCO + Dapper repository. Five sub-phases in least-coupled order.

**Module order:**
1. `Histo.Administration` (clsUser, LookupData) — 2 weeks
2. `Histo.AuditLog` (clsAuditLog) — 1 week
3. `Histo.QualityControl` (clsQCNote) — 1 week
4. `Histo.Histology` (clsBlock, clsHistology) — 2 weeks
5. `Histo.Submissions` (clsBatch, clsBatchSubmission, clsAnimal, clsTissue) — 3 weeks

**Go/no-go gate per module:** Repository integration tests pass against `Histology` database. Service unit tests pass with mocked repositories.

---

### Phase 5 — UI Migration (WebForms → Razor Pages)

**Duration:** 8 weeks  
**Purpose:** Convert all 64 ASPX pages and 8 ASCX controls to Razor Pages in `Histo.Web`.

**Batch order:**
1. ASCX controls → Partial Views / Layout (2 weeks)
2. 18 simple display/menu pages (1 week)
3. 28 standard CRUD pages (2 weeks)
4. 12 complex multi-step/copy workflows (2 weeks)
5. 6 report viewer pages (1 week)
6. Maintenance and admin pages (1 week)

**Go/no-go gate per batch:** Automated E2E tests pass for converted pages. `[Authorize]` policies enforce same access rules as legacy `CheckPermissions()`.

---

### Phase 6 — Infrastructure, CI/CD, and Cutover

**Duration:** 2 weeks  
**Purpose:** Provision Azure, establish full CI/CD pipeline, perform production cutover.

**Key deliverables:**
- Azure App Service, Azure SQL, Redis, Key Vault, Application Insights provisioned via Bicep
- Full GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline (build → test → publish → dev → UAT → prod)
- Blue-green cutover via App Service deployment slots
- Legacy IIS retained for 5 business days as rollback target

**Go/no-go gate:** Production smoke test passes. All three role groups sign in. One PDF report renders. Zero Application Insights exceptions after 30-minute soak.

---

## 5. Human-in-the-Loop Decision Points

The following steps **cannot be automated** and require human action before the next phase can proceed:

| Step | Phase | Owner | Blocker for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Azure admin creates Entra ID app registration + group IDs | Before Phase 2 | Azure admin | Phase 2 auth wiring |
| DB team confirms `GetUserByNTLogin` SP parameter strategy for Entra UPN vs NT login mapping | Before Phase 2 | DB team + Delivery Lead | Phase 2 auth equivalence |
| Extract stored procedure `.sql` files from `Histology` database using SSMS | Phase 0 | Developer | Phase 0 exit criteria |
| Populate Key Vault secrets (connection string, machineKey equivalent) after Phase 6 provisioning | Phase 6 | Platform engineer | Phase 6 cutover |
| Execute managed identity SQL grant in `Histology` database | Phase 6 | Azure admin / DBA | Phase 6 cutover |
| Configure GitHub environment protection rules (UAT and Production approval gates) | Phase 6 | Delivery Lead | Phase 6 deployment gates |
| Business stakeholder sign-off at each phase gate | Each phase | Named UAT representative | Each phase exit |

## 7. Definition of Done (Programme Level)

The migration programme is considered complete when:

1. All Phase 6 success criteria are met.
2. Legacy IIS server has been decommissioned (or placed on formal notice for decommission).
3. All ISS-* open issues in `migration-run-journal.md` are resolved or formally deferred to a post-migration backlog.
4. `docs/Runbook.md` is updated to reflect the Azure/container operational model.
5. The team has been briefed on Application Insights alerting and the on-call runbook for the new platform.
